match.reason: No existing point covers planning the specific resources a new business needs to start, such as premises, equipment, stock, staff and systems; the closest points only define a business or describe the establishment stage in general terms.

draft.title: Resources needed to start
card: A new business needs resources before it can trade. Planning them in advance helps the owner avoid running short once customers arrive.
Premises and equipment
the place where the business operates and the tools it uses, such as an oven, a van or a computer.
Stock and staff
stock is the goods held ready to sell or to use in making products. Staff are the people hired to do the work.
Systems
set ways of running the business, such as accounts to record money in and out, and a way to take orders and payments.
draft.remember: Plan premises, equipment, stock, staff and systems before opening, so the business does not run short.

a.q: Which item is a system that a new business needs?
opts: An accounts process that records money in and out
A van used to deliver orders to customers
A shop front rented on a busy street
A baker hired to work on weekends
a.why: Accounts are a set way of running the business, so they are a system. The van is equipment, the shop front is premises and the baker is staff.
a.clue: A system is a set way of working, not a thing or a person.

b.q: Mia opens a café in Dubbo. On day one she runs out of coffee beans and milk by 10 am. Which resource did she fail to plan enough of?
opts: Stock
Premises
Equipment
Staff
b.why: Coffee beans and milk are goods held ready to use in making products, so they are stock. She had premises and equipment to trade, but not enough stock to keep serving customers.
b.clue: Think about goods held ready to use or sell.

a.best: An accounts process that records money in and out

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about goods held ready to use or sell' repeats the card's definition of stock almost word for word, so it hands students the answer instead of hinting at it.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate and match the point. The only issue is that question b's clue restates the definition of stock, which gives the answer away.
